journeys.legacy_behavior: Startup displayed the complete resolved configuration before a real user-owned confirmation could create the working branch.
journeys.lean_behavior: Start persists and renders an unconfirmed card; only a current state-bound user event can confirm it and place the exact branch.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Users could review defaults, modify any startup selection, see the resulting configuration again, and explicitly recover or restart active work.
journeys.lean_behavior: Repository defaults only prefill the draft, configure consumes current input and redraws the card, while current and exit protect active state from overwrite.

journeys.legacy_behavior: The workflow preserved a deliberate Full or Focused choice and upgraded Focused work when material semantic risk appeared.
journeys.lean_behavior: The two paths retain distinct user stops and a user-owned semantic upgrade moves Focused work into Full specification without silently widening scope.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Full specification required iterative questioning with genuine answers, follow-up convergence, and complete critic coverage instead of a synthetic clear verdict.
journeys.lean_behavior: The Grill session allows one open question, requires at least one real answer and explicit convergence, then requires exactly one critic attempt; ordinary document edits do not create a critic retry loop.

journeys.legacy_behavior: The final specification was derived from the questioned requirement and retained a verifiable link to the converged Grill result and critic input.
journeys.lean_behavior: Digest receipts retain Grill, Spec, and critic versions for audit, while the final user confirmation binds the current documents without bouncing the workflow back for ordinary edits.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Full work produced a Design Story and required a bounded design or code review result before construction could rely on that design.
journeys.lean_behavior: Story remains a local recoverable artifact and review attempts occupy exact phase and checkpoint slots without recursive reviewer lifecycles.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Each construction checkpoint exposed its result for confirmation or revision and honored Continuous versus Staged commit timing.
journeys.lean_behavior: Checkpoint facts form a recoverable card, revisions revoke stale authorization, and Staged requires exact per-checkpoint receipts while Continuous defers one final commit.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Build, CodeCheck, and unit-test capabilities ran against explicit scope, recorded observable completion, and never retried invisibly after failure.
journeys.lean_behavior: Capability output stays opaque, each semantic slot has one automatic attempt, and an unchanged retry consumes an exact current user decision.

journeys.legacy_behavior: A defect discovered during Quality or Delivery reopened implementation and invalidated downstream conclusions that the repair could affect.
journeys.lean_behavior: User-owned repair events create a fresh Construction checkpoint and clear dependent quality and delivery authorization before revalidation.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Delivery separated startup-dirty ownership, exact business files, and independently selected conditional documents before staging or commit.
journeys.lean_behavior: The exact manifest authorizes only named files, dirty adoption is explicit, control files are excluded, and each conditional document needs its own selection fact.

journeys.legacy_behavior: User confirmation authorized one exact delivery plan while actual commit and push effects still had to be observed before completion.
journeys.lean_behavior: Confirmation binds the current nonempty manifest and push target, later mutation revokes it, and Hook observations complete exact commit and push receipts.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Interrupted work recovered deterministically, corrupt state produced actionable diagnostics, exit stayed available, and Windows paths and encodings remained supported.
journeys.lean_behavior: Current reads one authoritative state, corruption fails safely without guessing, exit is unconditional, and Windows identity plus process boundaries have native tests.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Unattended execution suppressed routine questions only within exact file and side-effect authorization and stopped safely on uncertainty or failure.
journeys.lean_behavior: Moonlight launch replaces routine Startup confirmation, but manifest subset checks, dirty ownership, conditional files, capability failures, and push retries remain fail-closed.

journeys.legacy_behavior: UT, CodeCheck, Grill, and Story could be invoked as scoped standalone specialist tools without creating a delivery workflow or hidden Git effects.
journeys.lean_behavior: The stateless toolbox keeps exact explicit scope, one-shot advisory semantics, interactive Grill shape, and local Story inputs without task-card protocols.

journeys.legacy_behavior: Cross-repository work enumerated repositories, ownership, touchpoints, contracts, dependencies, and reverse checks before one integrated confirmation.
journeys.lean_behavior: Recoverable Chain state requires complete repository ownership, three-angle analysis, contract error semantics, dependency evidence, and reverse verification.

journeys.legacy_behavior: A cross-repository session resumed from one explicit anchor, never guessed among stale files, and attributed answers and final confirmation to real current user input.
journeys.lean_behavior: The Chain pointer is authoritative and fail-closed, question answers are state-bound single-use events, and material changes invalidate the rendered confirmation digest.
